clusters.text: Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a suspect during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest. Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames. Difficult terrain was hindering efforts to extinguish the blaze and it was still burning early on Saturday, police said, with some 200 emergency personnel deployed. There were no reports of injuries. The Nazi dictator used the retreat, which lies above the town of Berchtesgaden, as a part-time seat of government and met commanders there to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941. Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature. A criminal investigation is under way to determine whether the suspect is connected to the fire. Completed by the Nazis in 1938, the Eagle's Nest escaped destruction after their defeat in 1945. Since then, it has become a popular tourist destination and houses a mountain inn. It serves as "a cautionary reminder of the abysses of the inhumane Nazi dictatorship", according to its official website , external . The rivalry between Barcelona and Real Madrid dates back to 1902, when the teams first met in the Copa de la Coronacion (a predecessor to the current-day Copa del Rey). Madrid and Barcelona are the two largest cities in Spain – this is at the root of their rivalry, which also has deep political undertones. In the 1930s, the divide between the two cities deepened. FC Barcelona, founded in 1899, came to symbolise Catalan independence, and Real, which came into existence three years later, represented Spanish nationalism. Securing our frontier model training environment
clusters.text: OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content “without risk of affecting external systems.” OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September, after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies, or swarm obscure websites. On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says. Even with these safeguards in place and no internet access, OpenAI found that agents “do not always need a network connection in order to communicate.” One test performed by the company asked AI models on separate virtual machines to exchange secrets without a network connection. To bypass this restriction, the AI agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache: > Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection. OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication. It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.” In the meantime, OpenAI says it will work to improve the security of its virtual machines, while testing for weaknesses in its testing environments. It’s also going to continue testing its monitoring systems, which were recently undermined by its AI agents during internal coding projects.

clusters.text: Real Madrid goalkeeper believes winning the Clasico at the Camp Nou would help send a strong message after being on a bad streak in the fixture in these last few years. Courtois was speaking to DAZN, where he was asked about the Clasico, and he was able to signify the importance of breaking the bad streak. He said: “Maybe there was a time when stars were missing from El Clasico, but now there are new players on the scene. We have Viní, Mbappé, Jude. They have Raphinha, Lamine, who is a fantastic player. It’s an intense rivalry. Over the last few years they have hurt us in some games, now it is time for us to respond. Winning at their ground would send a strong message.” Courtois also talked about respecting their rivals, and how players of the two teams differ in that sense. He said: “First of all, we have absolutely no problem saying the names of FC Barcelona players, that’s where I think we are different. It’s not a problem for us to praise someone, even if he is our rival. We respect players who are doing a good job, unlike the other side.” The Belgian goalkeeper was also asked about who he thinks should win the Ballon d’Or, to which he gave a very interesting response. He said: “What do we do? Do we pick someone who has won trophies, or someone who was above everyone else without winning? I am thinking of Kylian, individually, no one was better than Mbappé, but we didn’t win anything, he was fourth at World Cup… but he was outstanding. Lamine was less impressive than Kylian, but he became World Champion, won titles and had a great year.”

clusters.title: Ranchi Food Safety Raids Expose Major Violations
clusters.text: Food safety raids across Ranchi district have uncovered poor hygiene, improper labelling, invalid licences and suspected substandard paneer at more than 150 establishments inspected over the past month. Officials collected samples for laboratory testing, imposed fines on vendors and used mobile food-testing laboratories in Kanke and Lalpur as part of festive-season enforcement. The inspections covered all seven zones of the district, including Bundu. Food safety officers examined hotels, restaurants, street-food kitchens, retail outlets and market stalls. The violations recorded included missing or invalid food licences, inadequate kitchen hygiene and labelling that did not comply with prescribed requirements. In Kanke, officials found major violations involving food labels and hygiene conditions in hotel, restaurant and street-food kitchens. Paneer samples were also collected after officials raised concerns about their quality. “In Kanke, major violations included improper labelling, poor hygiene in hotel, restaurant and street food kitchens, and the absence of valid food licences. Paneer samples were also sent for testing on suspicion,” food safety officer Manoj Kumar said. The Lalpur zone, which includes Kokar, Morabadi and Lalpur, accounted for more than 65 inspections. Officials sent over 25 samples, including masala powders, paneer, cooking oil, sweets and ice creams, to the laboratory for analysis. Three laboratory reports have been received so far, and one paneer sample collected from a local retail shop failed to meet prescribed standards. “Further action will be taken based on the findings,” food safety officer Pawan Kumar said. The available laboratory results do not yet represent the entire district-wide inspection exercise, as testing of the remaining samples is pending. At the Morabadi vendor market, officials inspected 40 stalls and tested 22 samples. Two paneer samples failed quality checks, while industrial colouring agents were detected in two chaat samples. At least 25 vendors were fined Rs 500 each during the inspection. Officials also deployed the mobile food testing laboratory in Kanke and Lalpur. clusters.text: Prayagraj: The Sangam city has the potential to become one of the leading startup hubs in eastern Uttar Pradesh, said Sumit Rajesh Mahajan, CEO, UP Startup Mission.He said this while inaugurating Startup Confluence 2.0 at United Institute of Technology (UIT) on Friday.The two-day event is being organised by United Incubation Hub (UIH) at UIT.Mahajan said rapid advances in technologies such as artificial intelligence would make startups an important part of India’s future. clusters.title: Groups march in Ranchi seeking CEC’s resignation over SIR
clusters.text: Ranchi: Protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls continued in the city on Friday, with several student and youth organisations, women’s groups and trade unions marching from Ranchi University gate to Albert Ekka Chowk to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the exercise, “vote theft” and related issues.The demonstration, held on an all-India call by ‘People Against SIR’, saw participation from Citu, Jharkhand State Kisan Sabha, All India Lawyers Association, AISA, SFI and SUCI, among others. Protesters carried banners reading, “Har shahar Jantar Mantar, virodh hamara adhikar” (every town is now Jantar Mantar of Delhi, we have the right to protest), and demanded that Kumar be removed and prosecuted.Citu member Prakash Viplav said Election Commission should stop the SIR and ensure that no genuine voter is deprived of voting rights. Organisers claimed similar protests were held in at least a dozen districts and said the campaign would continue until EC answers concerns over transparency, alleged voter deletion and the claims and objections process in the state.The agitation comes amid a series of protests in Jharkhand over the SIR exercise. Congress workers had also marched to the CEO’s office in Dhurwa earlier this month, while RJD and AISA held separate protests seeking Kumar’s resignation and rollback of SIR. Earlier, Ranchi had emerged among urban seats with a high share of voters marked absent or untraceable during door-to-door verification, while subsequent SIR hearings saw long queues, confusion and anxious voters trying to secure their names on the final roll.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
